To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
afferent input regulates dendritic patterning through a rapid and reversible mechanism in the auditory brainstem of birds.

presynaptic afferent action potentials rapidly and locally regulate dendritic patternings of postsynaptic auditory neurons, whereas long-term maintenance of dendritic patterns may be correlated with the presence or absence of silent presynapses.

(1) action potential activity from the ipsilateral ear rapidly and reversibly induces retraction of ipsilateral dendrites of bipolar auditory neurons in the nucleus laminaris (a major nucleus of the auditory brain stem), and (2) this activity-induced retraction may be correlated with presynaptic cell death.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanisms underlying dendritic patterning in the central nervous system.
the development of a novel class of dendritic patterning in vivo and in vivo.
the development and plasticity of dendrites in the central nervous system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
afferent input can regulate dendritic patternings locally and globally through different mechanisms.

afferent action potentials regulate dendritic patternings of postsynaptic cells in a rapid, reversible, and compartment specific manner, and that this regulation is mediated by the presence of silent synapses.
the dendritic patterning in NL is controlled by afferent input, which regulates dendritic patterning through both global and local mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
dendrites of auditory neurons are dynamically regulated by afferent inputs in a way that reflects the activity of the presynaptic inputs.
dendritic patterning in NL is controlled by the presence of action potentials in the afferent axons. When action potentials are blocked,
the dendrites of auditory neurons are highly plastic, and that this plasticity can be regulated by afferent input.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local regulation of dendritic morphology by afferent input is a reversible process that is likely to play a role in the plasticity of dendrites.
dendritic patterning can be regulated in vivo by presynaptic activity.
the dendritic patterning and morphology of neurons can be dynamically regulated by the activity of their afferent inputs.
